Subject: Pulse pilot — short notice ask for slice rebalance + autoscale exception

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the great demo yesterday. We want to kick off a 3-week pilot (internal QA + closed beta) starting March 29 to validate latency at 99th percentile for a real-time triage feature. Based on our load tests, we expect two 2-hour daily windows where throughput spikes to ~250 qps and tail latency tightens.

Ask: can Redwood temporarily rebalance our Dedicated pool allocation (move ~8 GPU slices from the general pool to a 'pulse-pilot' slice) and grant an autoscaling policy exception to allow burst capacity above our configured cap for those two-hour windows? We understand this is an exception request and are open to any constraints (days, hours, max qps) that make this feasible.

I attached a simple projection (pulse_qps_projection.csv) and a short pilot scope doc. If helpful we can also share sanitized logs from our internal load tests.

High-level timeline:
- Pilot start: 2027-03-29
- Duration: 3 weeks
- Peak daily windows: 09:00-11:00 PT and 15:00-17:00 PT (approx)

Please let me know ASAP if this is viable and what info you need. We can be flexible on exact hours if it helps.

Best,
Alice
Product Lead, Integrations
Pulse Health

Kim / Marissa,

Quick read: feasible but with guardrails. Operational notes and options below.

1) Impact on reserved commitments
- Moving 8 slices out of the general pool is fine if we don't overlap with any hard-reserved customer windows. I checked the Q2 carveout calendar; there is headroom on weekdays for nights but afternoons are busier. We should gate the pilot to non-conflicting days or cap the burst so we never exceed 80% of the Dedicated pool during the requested windows.

2) Autoscale exception approaches
Option A (preferred): Create a time-limited policy that allows +30% burst above customer's cap only during the two windows. The runtime will prefer preemptible capacity first. We'll enforce an automatic rollback outside those windows.
Option B: Provision temporary preemptible slices in a separate burst lane tied to Pulse's tenant; quicker to stand up but slightly higher tail-latency risk.

3) Canary & smoke tests
- Strongly recommend a 1-hour canary on day 0 against a small routing subset (5% of traffic) and an automated health-check that triggers a rollback if 99th‑p99 latency degrades >40% relative to baseline. We can run that as part of the enablement.

4) Runbook / failure modes
- If we get contention with reserved workloads, our fallback is automatic model routing to a slightly lower-capacity variant (quantized model) with a permissive function-call to notify Pulse and switch back after 15 min. We'll include a kill-switch for on-call.

Estimate: Ops lift = 6–8 engineer-hours to configure policies, test canary, and instrument runbook. No infra purchases required if we accept Option A capped to +30% and strict windows. If Pulse requires sustained higher headroom we should discuss a short-term carveout contract.

I'll draft a short operations proposal.

— Jonas

Thanks Jonas — this looks reasonable. A few clarifications from product/pm side before we approve:

- Absolute SLOs: Pulse asked for p95 < 120ms and p99 < 450ms for the triage endpoint. We should make the p99 rollback threshold conservative (e.g., 350ms) to avoid bad customer experience.
- Duration: they said 3 weeks; propose we approve an initial 1-week trial (with two daily windows) and extend if metrics look good. This reduces risk and gives us a clearer cutover point.
- Telemetry: need to ensure Pulse will share anonymized trace samples for the canary so our regression alerts have signal.

If everyone is aligned I can send the pilot constraints back to Alice and propose the one-week trial with the canary and automatic rollback. Also request they sign a short pilot addendum that limits the exception window and liabilities.

— Marissa
